mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted as a shift toward restrictive policy, which raises the cost of capital and dampens equity valuation growth, thereby predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar tightening episodes, or the 20-day return exceeds -1% when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive triggered events, the 5-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 3% monthly suggests excess demand in the manufacturing sector, prompting firms to raise capital expenditures and expand output, which elevates equity valuations and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 5 prior similar acceleration episodes, the 60-day forward return mean was negative or non-significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three months indicates a cooling of demand pressures, reducing the likelihood of aggressive rate hikes and stabilizing investor expectations, which supports a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During 4 prior cooling episodes, the 20-day forward return mean was negative (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 0.2 percentage points while the federal funds rate remains below 2%, it suggests a shift toward accommodative policy, lowering real interest rates and stimulating equity market activity that drives positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 10 similar policy divergence events, the 20-day forward return mean is not positive (median ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged stagnation in job growth (PAYEMS) coupled with a rising labor force participation rate (not in catalog - use available proxies) — instead, use HOUST as proxy for participation — suggests underutilized workforce, which can indicate potential for wage growth and corporate optimism, predicting positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS flat for 3 months while HOUST increases by >1%
failure_condition: Over 8 similar underutilization events, the 5-day forward return mean is negative (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the goods price index (not in catalog — use INDPRO as proxy for inflation pressure from supply) followed by a sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests supply-side bottlenecks easing, which typically precedes a rally in equities and predicts positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth accelerates from <1% to >4% over 2 months
failure_condition: In 6 prior normalization episodes, the 60-day forward return mean was not statistically positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%), a sharp one-time drop in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% creates a 'soft landing' narrative that reduces policy uncertainty and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: In 7 prior low-inflation easing windows, the 20-day forward return mean was not positive (median ≤ 0).
